elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall..." — covers every covered expiry or termination without a narrowing trigger.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: "(i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months". The request condition is not tied only to anticipated expiry; it applies after any expiry or termination.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(ii) within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, return to Company all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Company" — the 30-day clock runs from termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: "(iii) after such return, delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion to Company in writing" — deletion and certification expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same inserted lead-in applies on expiry or termination of the Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six (6) months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Return of all Company data within thirty (30) days after expiry or termination in machine-readable format satisfies the export element.

reasons: The clause is genuinely missing: Sections 6(a), 6(b) and the duplicated 6(c) address only notice, final fees and assignment of Works in progress, with no data return, export, deletion or transition obligation anywhere in the cited text.

A single concise insertion carries all six preferred elements; no survival tail, at-own-expense language, extra remedies, procedures or boilerplate were added, and no existing favourable language was deleted or paraphrased.

Because "Customer Data" is undefined in this agreement, the drafter used "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Company", which captures every category of Company data rather than selected named types — appropriate and not an undefined trigger.

Intent is preserved: the fee-payment and Works-in-progress mechanics in 6(b) and 6(c), the 15-day notice rights, and Sections 4 and 8 are untouched and do not contradict the new paragraph; no dangling cross-references are created.

Placement between 6(b) and 6(c) leaves the inserted paragraph unlettered; purely cosmetic, but for tidiness the drafter may wish to letter it (e.g. as 6(d)) so subsequent cross-references remain unambiguous.
